assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and its translation into incretin therapies have transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit now emerging. Clear, original science (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, the active peptide) leading to major clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (biology and the therapeutic concept) and Mojsov (identification of the bioactive peptide) are the decisive scientific contributors; Knudsen is a major drug-development figure but the discovery-level credit is stronger for the three. Mojsov's credit has been contested and merits careful review.
assessment.maturity: Robustly confirmed by large randomized trials and wide clinical use; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Habener and other early contributors is disputed
Whether a prize should also honour the drug-development side (Knudsen) given the three-person limit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and that its blockade is clinically effective opened the biologic era for rheumatology and inflammatory bowel and skin disease. A paradigm of bench-to-bedside immunology with lasting impact; I note my own field but weigh it as I would any candidate.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini together defined the TNF-dependent cytokine cascade concept and led the first clinical trials; this pair is a coherent configuration. Contributions of antibody developers and other trialists are not credited in this list.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent confirmation and multiple approved agents.
uncertainties: Eligibility of each named person (including any who may have died) should be checked; I cannot verify this
Credit relative to antibody engineers and the TNF-cloning and cachexin literature

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, a fundamentally new therapeutic modality that has spawned an entire field with proof of concept now extending to autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CAR design with costimulation), June (clinical translation and CD19 CAR trials) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T cells) form a plausible three-way split; others such as Eshhar and Kuwana, Brenner and Dotti have claims not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Strong clinical confirmation across several approved products; long-term durability and safety still being defined, but the discovery is well established.
uncertainties: Attribution for first-generation CAR concept is not fully represented by the credited names
Rosenberg's contribution is partly distinct (TIL therapy) and may be viewed as a separate discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with light, an enabling method used across thousands of studies, with early clinical applications such as vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsin, and Deisseroth (with Boyden and others) demonstrated its use in neurons and built the tool-kit. Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck have genuine claims; six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit and make fair allocation difficult.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and fully mature as a methodology; the question is timing and which parts to honour.
uncertainties: Six credited names with contested priority among Boyden, Deisseroth, Miesenböck and the channelrhodopsin discoverers
Prizes for methods compared with discoveries of disease mechanism

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and the BCR-ABL inhibitor concept turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease to a manageable one and established molecularly targeted cancer therapy as a paradigm.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof in CML) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and further clinical work) are the natural trio; Rowley, Nowell and others contributed the underlying genetics but are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature and thoroughly confirmed, with long-term survival data; recognition is well past due and the field has been widely honoured by other prizes.
uncertainties: Role of upstream BCR-ABL genetics (Philadelphia chromosome, Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) relative to this credited set
Sawyers' contribution is more on resistance than on the original discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Human genetics identified PCSK9 as a regulator of LDL receptor levels, and inhibitors now lower LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular events. This is a clear case of genetics validating a therapeutic target.
assessment.attribution: Seidah (identification and biochemistry of PCSK9), Hobbs and Cohen (loss-of-function variants and cardiovascular protection) are the best-supported trio; Abifadel and Boileau first reported gain-of-function mutations in familial hypercholesterolemia, so credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by outcome trials and clinical use; timely though not as broad in impact as incretin therapy.
uncertainties: Priority of Abifadel and Boileau for the original disease gene is an unresolved allocation issue
Therapeutic antibodies and siRNA development are not credited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune and interferon responses, linking infection, autoimmunity (including interferonopathies and lupus-related disease), cancer immunity and senescence. Original and mechanistically clear, with broad conceptual reach.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP; Barber and Ishikawa identified STING. Together these are decisive contributions; Sun and Wu were key coauthors but the senior roles are better reflected in the named three.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely and mechanistically stable, though clinical translation (STING agonists and antagonists) is still immature, which may make recognition slightly early.
uncertainties: Role of Vance, Tsuchiya and others in STING biology is not credited here

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of IL-6 as a B-cell differentiation factor, cloning of it and its receptor, and development of tocilizumab established IL-6 blockade for rheumatoid arthritis, giant cell arteritis, cytokine release syndrome and other conditions. Clear originality with substantial clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano led the discovery, cloning and receptor work in Osaka, forming a coherent two-person configuration; antibody humanization teams are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Mature and well confirmed with multiple approved agents; recognition is timely though it competes with TNF blockade in the same therapeutic domain.
uncertainties: Overlap with the TNF candidate in the autoimmunity field could limit the chance of both being honoured together
Contributions of others who cloned IL-6 independently (for example as interferon-beta2 or hybridoma growth factor)
